result.title: DriveMLP: When Training Strategy Outperforms Model Complexity in Autonomous Driving
result.comment: Accepted at 2026 Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)
result.summary: Learning motion planning policies that remain reliable under closed-loop execution is a central challenge in Autonomous Driving (AD). Imitation Learning (IL) scales well to large AD datasets but suffers from distribution shift, causal confusion, and compounding errors under closed-loop execution. In contrast, Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically requires handcrafted rule-based rewards and massive simulation. We study a simple closed-loop IL framework that uses RL purely as an optimization tool, guided by a trajectory-distance reward derived from logged expert data. We refer to this training strategy as Expert-Guided RL (EGRL). Through a controlled empirical study we find evidence that the training procedure, rather than model size and complexity, accounts for a substantial part of the performance gains. We then introduce DriveMLP, a lightweight MLP policy trained with EGRL, as a simple instantiation of these findings. It achieves a score of 86.51 on the nuPlan Val14 Reactive benchmark, a +3.2 point improvement over the previous best IL planner (Flow Planner), with >15x faster inference. Code is available at: https://github.com/alessandro-canevaro/DriveMLP .

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究自动驾驶闭环运动规划，提出以专家轨迹距离为奖励、把 RL 仅作优化工具的 EG RL 训练策略，并据此构造轻量 MLP 规划器 DriveMLP，论证训练流程比模型规模更决定性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 属于自动驾驶策略学习与闭环评测，既未涉及多模态推理的内部状态、视觉证据使用或 latent 生成，也未提供可直接核查的 latent 推理方法线索，故不入选。
